author: Tim
title: Fans Shocked After Stevie Wonder Addresses Vision Claims
text:
Stevie Wonder finally decided to say something about the long-time rumors that he’s not really blind. He brought it up on stage during a stop in Cardiff on his Love, Light and Song tour.
He said: “I must say to all of you, something that I was thinking, ‘When did I want to let the world know this?’ But I wanted to say it right now. You know there have been rumors about me seeing and all that? But seriously, you know the truth.”
Then he cleared it up. He said: “Truth is, shortly after my birth, I became blind. Now, that was a blessing because it’s allowed me to see the world in the vision of truth, of sight. See people in the spirit of them, not how they look. Not what color they are, but what color is their spirit?”
Stevie wasn’t actually born blind. He lost his sight at around six weeks old because of a condition called retinopathy of prematurity, or ROP.
He was born premature and spent time in an incubator, and there was too much oxygen in there which caused the damage. That’s how ROP happens, and it can lead to blindness if not caught early.
Some people might recognize the name of that condition if they’ve dealt with it or heard about it before. It causes abnormal blood vessels to grow in the eye, and without treatment, it can cause serious vision loss.
The whole seeing rumor has been around for a while, but one thing that gave it new life was a story told by Shaquille O’Neal. He said they both lived in the same building in Los Angeles and had a weird elevator moment.
While the valets were taking care of Stevie’s car, he made his way to the lobby where Shaq was already in the elevator. And this is where it got strange.
O’Neal said: “He comes in, says ‘what’s up Shaq’. Presses the button, it’s a true story, presses the button, gets off on his floor by himself, goes to his room. I went and called every person I knew and told the story. They didn’t believe me.”
That story kept the rumors going, but Stevie’s recent statement might finally put it to rest. Or maybe not, since people always like to believe what they want.
